items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: And at this time we had a guy sitting in with us who played with Earl Hines. His name was Ed Fant.

ctx.x: That's right, you know. I wasn't

supposed to be there but I was there and I'll tell you about the time Murray McEachern came to the Three Deuces and he wanted to hear Art, and he just got in from Canada and he was afraid to bring his trombone in so he checked his trombone in the check room and came in. And at this time we had a guy sitting in with us who played with Earl Hines. His name was Ed Fant. And he was a trombone player. And Murray heard -- this is a black guy, Eddie Fant, and Murray heard Fant play and he broke that checkroom door down…

So consequently Benny Goodman heard him playing down there because he used to come very night, and this is how Benny Goodman hired him, and this is why he hired him. He heard him at the Three Deuces. Benny was playing at the Congress Hotel then, I believe. Yes, and this is how I first met Murray McEachern. See, I think Murray can attest to the fact that I exist, you know, we played together then --
